A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark-saturation study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original analysis of 60 benchmarks, including saturation prevalence, associations with benchmark properties, and Bayesian regression results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original analyses and adds parameter-sensitivity results and benchmark-level case studies.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same normalized top-model score spread, effective sample-size formula, and exponential saturation index, with defaults k=5 and alpha=0.5. V2's stabilization footnote and expanded explanations do not establish a procedural change to the retained analysis.

E1.justification: Table 3 retains the same 60 benchmark entries, with unchanged task and language coverage. The new sensitivity analyses and case studies reuse this corpus.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing saturation-measurement methods against the proposed index. The leaderboard model examples also match between v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 6; alternative parameter settings are internal sensitivity checks.

E3.justification: V2 adds a sensitivity protocol comparing k=3 versus 5 and alpha=0.5 versus 0 or 1, using Spearman correlation and saturation-bin agreement. The default analysis settings, collection period, and annotation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 2.3 adds focused checks of the index's sensitivity to two parameters. Appendix E adds five worked case studies examining score compression, stagnation, and saturation in dynamically updated benchmarks. The existing hypothesis and regression analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 defines the standard-error estimator; v2 Table 7 additionally reports benchmark-specific estimates, including SE_delta=0.0338 for the previously reported Math-500 scores. Existing standard-deviation error bars and posterior credible intervals remain unchanged, with no additional runs or seeds reported.

E6.justification: The main results remain unchanged, including 29 of 60 benchmarks having high or very high saturation and Bayesian R-squared of 0.884 ± 0.012. V2 adds sensitivity correlations of 0.88–0.92, bin agreement of 18.3–48.3%, a benchmark-level ranking in Figure 1, and numerical case-study results in Table 7.

T1.justification: The boxed definition replaces the requirement that future improvements are impossible with further improvements being statistically indistinguishable under the evaluation protocol. This revises the formal criterion; the index equations remain equivalent, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and principal findings about saturation prevalence, age, scale, and limited protection from private test sets. The new conclusion restates these claims, while the explicit H6 statement concerns templating already analyzed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit qualifications about causal identification, selective leaderboard reporting, evolving benchmark protocols, and metric-specific uncertainty requirements. Appendix E adds benchmark-specific interpretations, including saturation despite dynamic updates; its claim that TruthfulQA's spread exceeds uncertainty conflicts with Table 7.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents epsilon stabilization near zero uncertainty, expands the description of annotated quality issues, and supplies additional benchmark sample counts in Table 7. The annotation schema, existing example metadata, and code/data repository target remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds OpenAI's report on discontinuing SWE-bench Verified evaluation and discusses its implications for evaluation artifacts and training exposure. Research positioning otherwise remains stable; most reference changes update metadata or consolidate existing citations.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the narrative, including the abstract, subdivided conceptual framework, grouped empirical discussion, and expanded recommendations. It moves related work to Appendix A and adds a roadmap, conclusion, conflict-of-interest disclosure, and author contribution statement.

P2.justification: V2 adds the ranked overview figure and sensitivity and case-study tables, extends the hypothesis table, removes v1 Table 2, and reorders the example tables. All five existing plots retain their graphics, with relocation, renumbering, and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: The revised protocol-relative definition, sensitivity tests, and clearer metric and causal limitations make the central index more transparent and assessable. These gains outweigh limited new interpretation problems, but do not establish comprehensive validation: Table 1 shows only 18.3–48.3% bin agreement, and Appendix E incorrectly says TruthfulQA's spread exceeds uncertainty despite R_norm=0.7766.
